title: Rectification of a homotopy square by mapping-path objects
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, Kan complexes, internal functor simplicial sets, homotopy fibers and geometric realization as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $X,Y,S,T$ be Kan complexes, with maps $r:X\to S$, $q:Y\to T$, $u:X\to Y$, $v:S\to T$ and a specified simplicial homotopy $H:X\times\Delta^1\to T$ from $qu$ to $vr$. Set
$$E_r=X\times_{S,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,S),\qquad E_q=Y\times_{T,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,T).$$
Write $e_r:E_r\to X$, $e_q:E_q\to Y$ for the projections and $R:E_r\to S$, $Q:E_q\to T$ for terminal evaluation. The two maps on the edges $01$ and $12$ given respectively by $H\circ(e_r\times\mathrm{id})$ and by applying $v$ to the universal path of $E_r$ define a map $E_r\times\Lambda^2_1\to T$. It extends to a simplicial map $C:E_r\times\Delta^2\to T$. For every such extension, its $02$ edge $c$ defines a simplicial map $U=(u e_r,c):E_r\to E_q$ satisfying
$$e_qU=ue_r,\qquad QU=vR.$$
For each vertex $s\in S$ its restriction $R^{-1}(s)\to Q^{-1}(v(s))$ is a model of the homotopy-fiber map for the specified homotopy $H$: at $(x,\gamma)$ its path is the coherent composite of $H_x$ with $v\gamma$, witnessed by $C$. If $C_0,C_1$ are two extensions of this same horn map, there is a simplicial homotopy between them relative to $E_r\times\Lambda^2_1$; its $02$ edge gives a homotopy between $U_0,U_1$ for which the projection to $Y$ is constantly $ue_r$ and the projection to $T$ is constantly $vR$. In particular it restricts on every strict fiber to a homotopy of the fiber maps. For a vertex $(x,\gamma)$, the realized path $c_{(x,\gamma)}$ is homotopic relative to endpoints to the concatenation $|H_x|\cdot|v\gamma|$. No weak-equivalence hypothesis on $u$ or $v$, and no fibration hypothesis on $r$ or $q$, is imposed; empty complexes and fibers are permitted.

source.place: Corollaries 2.3.2.2 and 2.3.2.4, printed pp. 100-101 (PDF pp. 117-118): parameterized coherent composition and its relative uniqueness. Agent-formulated application to mapping-path objects; not an assertion that HTT states this square verbatim. Online source read; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial comparison.

from.place: Proof paragraph 2, finite coefficient mapping-complex adjunction before R lim, via lem-coef-algebroid-presentability: the mapping-space comparison for the transported fiber colimit is an equivalence because its base comparison and every homotopy-fiber comparison are equivalences. Auxiliary strictification needed before the homotopy-fiber detection argument: replace the specified homotopy square by a strict mapping-path square, including coherent fiber maps and independence of composite fillers.
